gauge.name: Little Blue River near Barnes

impacts.statement: The intersection of highway 148 and 15th Road in Washington county floods.
Kansas Highway 148 bridge deck floods, 4.5 miles north of Barnes.
Top rail of the Sunflower Road Bridge is inundated by flood waters in Marshall county.
Sunflower Road bridge deck floods over the Little Blue River. Flood waters reach the low steel of the Kansas Highway 148 bridge, 4.5 miles north of Barnes.
Sunflower Road floods about 250 feet east of the Little Blue River in Marshall county. Farm field, 4.5 miles north of Barnes, floods north of the river and west of Highway 148 in Washington county.
Minor flooding of farm fields along the Little Blue River...south of the Sunflower Road Bridge in Marshall county.
Farm field, 4.5 miles north of Barnes, south of the river and east of Highway 148 floods.
Farm field, 4.5 miles north of Barnes, on the west side of Highway 148 floods north of the river.
Lowland agricultural flooding occurs from 15th Road and Zenith Road in Washington County to Waterville in Marshall County.

value.label: North American Vertical Datum of 1988
value.description: A fixed reference for elevations determined by geodetic leveling. The datum was derived from a general adjustment of the first-order terrestrial leveling nets of the United States, Canada, and Mexico. In the adjustment, only the height of the primary tidal bench mark, referenced to the International Great Lakes Datum of 1985 (IGLD 85) local mean sea level height value, at Father Point, Rimouski, Quebec, Canada was held fixed, thus providing minimum constraint. NAVD 88 and IGLD 85 are identical. However, NAVD 88 bench mark values are given in Helmert orthometric height units while IGLD 85 values are in dynamic heights. See International Great Lakes Datum of 1985, National Geodetic Vertical Datum of 1929, and geopotential difference. NAVD 88 should not be used as Mean Sea Level.

gauge.forecastReliability: Forecasts are issued as needed during times of high water, but are not routinely available.
